Laminar is an reinforcement learning RL post-training framework for LLMs and long-horizon agents. The core idea is simple: stop forcing every trajectory and every GPU to wait for the slowest one. For teams training coding agents with long, skewed rollouts, that is where most GPU time goes. TL;DR What: A framework. Tested on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (30.5B total, 3.3B active) and Qwen2.5 at 7B, 32B and 72B. Runs on: Multi-node NVIDIA GPU clusters with Ray and CUDA. Best: 52.2% on SWE-bench Verified, up from 46.6% for the base model. Worst: Early repo (1 commit at launch), vLLM is the only listed inference backend, and per-step async checkpointing is still in progress. Bottom line: Best: fewer samples and GPU-hours to a higher SWE-bench score. Worst: the headline comparison mixes H800 and H100 hardware. What is Laminar? Laminar is an asynchronous RL post-training framework that decouples rollout, buffering, training and weight transfer into independent loops. It is built on verl and Uni-Agent and released under Apache-2.0. The launch blog splits the stack into 3 layers. verl provides training and inference compute backends. Uni-Agent handles agent execution, tool calls and sandboxes. Laminar handles cluster-scale orchestration. How does Laminar’s architecture work? The design rests on 3 principles: full decoupling, fine-grained asynchrony and fault tolerance. Rollout loop: Drives agent interactions and serves generation across inference replicas. Experience buffer (data plane): Separates trajectory production from training and serves ready batches on demand. Training loop: Samples batches, computes advantages and off-policy corrections, and publishes weights. Weight Relay (weight plane): The trainer stages weights into per-node shared CPU memory and keeps going. Replicas pull updates on their own schedule. In the research paper , relays are CPU processes, 1 per rollout machine. They broadcast weights along a pipelined RDMA chain. A 72B model reaches 127 other relays in under 1.6 seconds. What is version-consistent rollout? Most async systems use version-mixed partial rollout. They interrupt in-flight trajectories at each weight update and resume under the new policy. That forces repeated re-prefill. Laminar also supports a version-consistent mode. Each trajectory finishes under 1 policy version. Replicas update independently, without a global weight-switch barrier. The blog states that this keeps the prefix KV cache intact. It argues re-prefill cost scales cubically with sequence length under frequent updates. Repack handles the tail. Once new weights exist, leftover old-version trajectories are consolidated onto fewer replicas. Drained replicas then load the new version immediately. How does Laminar perform on SWE-bench Verified? The research team trained Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on SWE-rebench. They evaluated on all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks with greedy decoding. Base model: 46.6% (233/500). Baseline peak (step 150, 64x H100): 51.4% with 76.4k samples and 5,085 GPU-hours. Laminar match (step 320, 64x H800): 51.4% with 41.0k samples (46% fewer) and 1,450 GPU-hours (71% fewer). Laminar peak (step 400, 64x H800): 52.2% with 51.2k samples (33% fewer) and 1,843 GPU-hours (64% fewer). How does Laminar handle failures? Faults stay local. If a rollout replica fails, the router fences only that replica. It restarts, reloads weights from the local relay and resumes from its generated token prefix. A replica that fails during weight loading recovers without blocking the trainer. Trainer checkpoints align model state, prompt cursors and published weight versions. laminar.eval also evaluates several checkpoints at once across resident replicas, in batch or streaming mode during training. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.&nbsp;</p> <p>Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.&nbsp;</p> <p>While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture.&nbsp;<a href="https://www.pingidentity.com/en/company/championing-every-identity.html">We champion every identity.</a> One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.&nbsp;</p> <p>We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.&nbsp;</p></div><p>As a Professional Services Engagement Manager, you will report to the Director of Professional Services and will play an essential role in Professional Services' commitment to deliver successfully on engagements striving for predictability, repeatability and financial responsibility. We are looking for someone who enjoys leading engagements for external clients and one who can manage a portfolio of complex projects. This is a hybrid role that will require 50% of your time to be spent in hands-on project management and 50% of the time to be spent in services sales. You will have several years of experience in project management best practices, consulting, and leading technology implementation projects. You will join a highly effective team with a focus towards team work, successful deployments and outstanding cooperation with our go-to-market teams. Our goal is not just to make our customers successful, but to take your project management skillset to the next level.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>You will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Be the primary point of contact overseeing engagements delivered by Ping Professional Services.</li> <li>Build relationships with customers, partners, and our go-to-market teams</li> <li>Manage a portfolio of projects for successful delivery outcomes, revenue and profitability.</li> <li>Manage outcomes to resolve issues, conflicts, risks, and dependencies</li> <li>Flourish in a collaborative environment, demonstrating teamwork and excellence</li> <li>Provide written/verbal status updates to customer, partners and leadership on key project metrics</li> <li>Support revenue forecasting, invoicing and resourcing efforts for the Professional Services team</li> <li>Be an active member of project governance setup</li> <li>Support new services sales effort by attaching professional services offerings to new deals.</li> <li>Establish, monitor and manage own services sales pipeline</li> <li>Participate in regional license and services sales forecasting</li> <li>Define and present business value of services deals</li> <li>Scope complex custom services engagements together with technical consultants</li> <li>Understand and apply meaningful commercial incentives for services deals</li> </ul> <p><strong>Requirements:&nbsp;</strong></p> <p><strong>You have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5 years of project management experience in consulting and technology implementation</li> <li>Motivated and comfortable adapting to change and competing demands with timelines</li> <li>Bachelor's Degree</li> <li>Exceptional skills around communications and delivery</li> <li>Can independently deliver implementations</li> <li>PMP Certification</li> <li>Business or technology consulting background</li> <li>Experience motivating teams</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here.
